question: Go/no-go 2: does a range-aware arm (R5, R6) that lowers the range-error tail at comparable MAE (S4) also improve the proton gamma pass rate over R3, and is the gain more than the per-tissue bias correction R4? Secondary: does the per-ray WET error track proton dose?

cases.stratify: region (largest-remainder allocation), hashed order within region
cases.pool: development cases with an out-of-fold R3 prediction for seed 0; test cases are never loaded

aggregation: per-case metrics averaged over seeds before testing

plans.target: sphere at the body centroid (SynthRAD2025 releases no PTV), same as the range harness
plans.outside_body: set to air in the reference CT and in every sCT
plans.angle_convention: sctrange projector (0 travels +y, 90 travels +x); pyRadPlan gantry = (360 - angle) mod 360
plans.objectives: target squared deviation to the prescription (priority 800), body squared overdosing above 50 % (priority 10)
plans.optimised_on: reference CT; the same weights are recomputed on every sCT and on the reference CT (forward engine)
plans.engine: pyRadPlan default proton (Generic) and photon (Generic) machines and HLUT

gamma.normalisation: global, maximum of the reference recomputation

test: one-sided paired Wilcoxon (method arm > comparator) over the dosimetry cases; Holm over the four comparisons

verdicts.GO: some method arm beats R3 and R4 on target CVaR90 in S4 (MAE condition met) and beats R3 on proton gamma 2%/2mm here
verdicts.RANGE GAIN WITHOUT DOSE CONFIRMATION: some method arm beats R3 and R4 on target CVaR90 in S4, but none beats R3 on proton gamma
verdicts.RIGHT ESTIMATOR SUFFICES: some method arm beats R3 on target CVaR90 in S4, none beats R4
verdicts.NO-GO: no method arm beats R3 on target CVaR90 in S4
verdicts.NOT EVALUATED: no S4 verdict on real data

proxy.unit: case-level pairs are (case, arm) after seed averaging, bulk density included; bootstrap resamples cases

verdicts.VALIDATED: case Spearman >= 0.5 with 95 % CI above 0, partial Spearman given MAE with CI above 0, and ray Spearman(dWET, -dR80) >= 0.7
verdicts.PARTIAL: only the case-level or only the ray-level criterion holds

secondary: photon gamma pass rates of every arm (expected near 100 %: photons are insensitive to SPR errors)
proton gamma of R1 versus R3 (Proposition 5 in dose), two-sided
target D95, D2 and mean dose differences by arm and region
Theil-Sen slope of dR80 on dWET (expected about -1 / SPR at the distal edge)
